title: Grateful Dead Live at Kresge Plaza, Massachusetts Institute of Technology on 1970-05-06
venue: Kresge Plaza, Massachusetts Institute of Technology
source: MSR (MIT Reels) 1/2 Track Mono -> Otari MX 55 2 track (playback) -> TC 2000 Studio Effects Processor (using only the A->D converter, no effects) ->Sonic Solutions (at 20 bits resolution) -> mastered to CD using Sony SBM 2(No DAT generations) -> CD (from Gans) > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: A raw yet clear soundboard capture of a searing, politically‑charged show highlighted by an incendiary “Dancing in the Streets” and a soaring “Morning Dew”.
ai_review.review: The May 6, 1970 MIT performance is consistently praised as one of the band’s most intense and historically charged shows – the crowd‑fuelled anger after Kent State erupts into blistering versions of “Dancing in the Streets”, “Not Fade Away” and a transcendent “Morning Dew”.  The recording is a mono soundboard feed that, while showing distortion, mic dropouts and occasional rawness, remains surprisingly sharp and listenable, making the set’s power come through clearly.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive comments about the musical performance (≈4.8/5) and a generally good but imperfect soundboard recording (≈3.8/5) combine to a weighted average of ~4.5 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mono soundboard feed with noticeable distortion, mic drop‑outs (e.g., Pigpen on “Good Lovin’”) and occasional rawness, but overall clear, sharp and well balanced for a 1970 capture.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is described as a hot, angry, and tightly focused performance driven by the political climate; transitions are tight and the energy stays high throughout, making the show feel like a single, powerful statement.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s SG thrashes on “Dancing in the Streets” and his tone is praised as alive and intense.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh delivers one of his most devastating bass runs, especially highlighted during the climax of “Dancing in the Streets”.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals are noted in the context of the band’s split‑off announcement after “Not Fade Away”.
